claims.claim: IBM Q2 2026 revenue was $17.2B, up 1% YoY, while Software grew 5%, Red Hat 11% and Data 19%; management expects 4%-5% constant-currency full-year revenue growth.

IBM is increasing AI/quantum optionality through watsonx/Red Hat/HashiCorp/Confluent and plans more than $10B of quantum investment over five years, while targeting a fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2029.

risks.risk: Overall growth remains modest, acquisition spending has reduced cash balances, and legacy infrastructure/transaction-processing exposure can offset AI growth.

contradictions.contradiction: Strong AI/quantum strategic positioning coexists with only 1% reported Q2 revenue growth and declines in Infrastructure and Transaction Processing.

unknowns.unknown: Incremental revenue directly attributable to current AI offerings is not quantified in this artifact.

claims.claim: IBM maintained free-cash-flow growth expectations and raised constant-currency revenue expectations to 4%-5%, but Q2 revenue growth was only 1%, making execution mixed rather than uniformly strong.
The execution test is conversion of AI-ready software and quantum investment into sustained higher growth while preserving cash generation after substantial acquisition spending.

risks.risk: Acquisition integration, debt and slow legacy segments can dilute returns from AI/quantum investment.

contradictions.contradiction: Raised full-year expectations contrast with weak reported Q2 top-line growth, requiring follow-through in subsequent quarters.

unknowns.unknown: Current valuation and acquisition-adjusted organic growth remain for Alpha underwriting.
